anti_generic_signature_read: Round 2, unprimed, on the rim: "The edge treatment reads as flame - tapering, rounded-tipped, curling licks of fire, now flickering in inconsistent directions the way real flames do, rather than the raked pinwheel vanes I took them for before." Round 2's reason: "Blades with mixed, unrelated rake angles cannot be teeth, vanes or blades in any working sense - a saw, a ratchet, a turbine or an impeller all require a single consistent rake, and mixed rake is the one thing that positively rules those out."

largest_risk: Fidelity to the hand-made concept, which this Wish's own fixed values now bound. Shown the concept and both builds at matched scale, the critic put this build closer than the one it corrects on root width, body fullness, handedness and length spread, and further away on count: "I count roughly sixteen licks per third in the concept band, i.e. something in the mid-to-high forties around the ring. The 48-flame build matched the concept's density almost exactly; 32 is a visible thinning ... If fidelity to the concept were the only criterion, 48 was the better number." It named three things neither build captures: the concept's recurved hooked tips ("the single most characteristic thing about the hand-made original"), its fused undulating collar, and its engraved interior veins - "the built rim still reads as a repeated part and the concept reads as drawn." None is actionable here: the Wish fixes the count at 32, forbids the fused collar outright, and carries over the approved flame curve and CORONA_TURN_EXP 1.15 that a recurved hook or an interior vein would change. They are recorded for the next brief. The second risk is that the centre bar is unmarked on the object itself, so the capture reads from an annotated sheet rather than from the part; the hub is carried-over geometry this correction may not cut into.
resolution: One critic, four review rounds, on this build's own images; no review from the set being corrected is reused. Round 1, unprimed, answered SUN and read the rim as flame but reported "a consistent counterclockwise sweep around the disc, like a pinwheel", failing acceptance clause 1. That drove repair 1. The measured split was already a correct 14 against 18; the fault was legibility. Visible rake scales with flame length, so only the eight tall flames carry it at a glance, and under the first walk constant those eight fell into same-sign pairs - a period-4 sweep in exactly the flames the eye reads. Only the walk constant moved, frac(sqrt(19)/2) to frac(sqrt(117)/2); generator, run caps, minority share and run bounds unchanged, and the tall flames now differ from their tall neighbour at six of eight steps. Round 2, unprimed, retracted the pinwheel verdict as "clearly false" and diagnosed its own error unprompted: it had judged rake in image space, valid only at 12 o'clock. Round 3 revealed the Wish and put every requirement separately, and resolved three held items - two were faults in the questions put to the critic, including requirement 2, re-answered MATCHES once the correct 48-flame baseline was supplied. Round 4 read the signature sheet twice: the critic had misread the counter parked on the centre bar as a dropped part and held that flag through two rounds. That drove repair 2, which touched no geometry. Final verdict: "No. Nothing on this sheet is blocking, and nothing in the geometry ever was." Since repair 1 only snap/signature.png changed; the geometry and all twelve other canonical renders are byte-identical to what rounds 1 and 2 read. Four round-2 findings were retracted as the critic's own errors under measurement, a fifth as a resampling artifact. print_gate_sha256s is empty and the product is sealed digitally-verified-not-print-ready with print_ready_claim false. Motion is unverified: no coupled mechanism, and the operator's option disables it.
reviewer: independent native critic subagent af452d87837086278, given image paths and a fixed answer schema only. Rounds 1-2 unprimed, 3-4 primed. Protocol in BLIND-REVIEWS.md.
